import pandas as pd

# Load all source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_7/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_7/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_7/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_7/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_7/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_7/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_7/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source6_7_0 and Source6_7_1 on 'Id'
df_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="Id", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Step 2: Join Source6_7_2 and Source6_7_3 on 'Id'
df_23 = pd.merge(source2, source3, on="Id", suffixes=('_x_3', '_y_4'))

# Rename columns of df_23 to match target schema suffixes
df_23.rename(columns={
    'SalePrice_x_3': 'SalePrice_x_3',
    'SalePrice_y_4': 'SalePrice_y_4'
}, inplace=True)

# Step 3: Join Source6_7_4 and Source6_7_5 on 'Id'
df_45 = pd.merge(source4, source5, on="Id", suffixes=('_x_5', '_y_6'))

# Rename columns of df_45 to match target schema suffixes
df_45.rename(columns={
    'SalePrice_x_5': 'SalePrice_x_5',
    'SalePrice_y_6': 'SalePrice_y_6'
}, inplace=True)

# Step 4: Join Source6_7_6 and Source6_7_1 on 'Id'
df_61 = pd.merge(source6, source1, on="Id", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Rename columns of df_61 to match target schema suffixes
df_61.rename(columns={
    'SalePrice_x': 'SalePrice_x_5',  # Source6_7_6 SalePrice renamed to SalePrice_x_5 (to match target)
    'SalePrice_y': 'SalePrice_y_6'   # Source6_7_1 SalePrice renamed to SalePrice_y_6 (to match target)
}, inplace=True)

# But from the intermediate_step4 example, SalePrice_x_5 and SalePrice_y_6 come from this join,
# and SalePrice column is from Source6_7_6 (SalePrice_x renamed to SalePrice_x_5),
# SalePrice_y_6 from Source6_7_1 (SalePrice_y renamed to SalePrice_y_6),
# and SalePrice column is also present in intermediate_step4 but NaN, so we will keep SalePrice from source1 as SalePrice_y_6.

# Actually, from the intermediate_step4 schema:
# ['Id', 'SalePrice_x', 'SalePrice_y', 'SalePrice_x_3', 'SalePrice_y_4', 'SalePrice', 'SalePrice_x_5', 'SalePrice_y_6']
# SalePrice column is present but NaN, so we will keep SalePrice from source6 as SalePrice (final SalePrice).

# To avoid confusion, let's rename columns in df_61 as:
df_61.rename(columns={
    'SalePrice_x': 'SalePrice_x_5',
    'SalePrice_y': 'SalePrice_y_6'
}, inplace=True)

# Add SalePrice column from source6 (which is SalePrice_x in df_61 before rename)
df_61['SalePrice'] = source6.set_index('Id').loc[df_61['Id'], 'SalePrice'].values

# Now we have four intermediate dataframes:
# df_01 with SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y
# df_23 with SalePrice_x_3, SalePrice_y_4
# df_45 with SalePrice_x_5, SalePrice_y_6
# df_61 with SalePrice_x_5, SalePrice_y_6, SalePrice

# We need to join all these on 'Id' to get the final target table.

# First, join df_01 and df_23 on 'Id'
df_0123 = pd.merge(df_01, df_23[['Id', 'SalePrice_x_3', 'SalePrice_y_4']], on='Id', how='inner')

# Then join df_0123 and df_45 on 'Id'
df_012345 = pd.merge(df_0123, df_45[['Id', 'SalePrice_x_5', 'SalePrice_y_6']], on='Id', how='inner')

# Finally, join df_012345 and df_61 on 'Id'
# But df_45 and df_61 both have SalePrice_x_5 and SalePrice_y_6 columns, so to avoid conflict,
# we will drop SalePrice_x_5 and SalePrice_y_6 from df_61 before join and keep SalePrice column from df_61.

df_61_reduced = df_61[['Id', 'SalePrice']]

final_df = pd.merge(df_012345, df_61_reduced, on='Id', how='inner')

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['Id', 'SalePrice_x', 'SalePrice_y', 'SalePrice_x_3', 'SalePrice_y_4', 'SalePrice_x_5', 'SalePrice_y_6', 'SalePrice']

final_df = final_df[['Id', 'SalePrice_x', 'SalePrice_y', 'SalePrice_x_3', 'SalePrice_y_4',
                     'SalePrice_x_5', 'SalePrice_y_6', 'SalePrice']]

# Save the final dataframe to the target path
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_7/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
s0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_7/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
s1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_7/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
s2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_7/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
s3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_7/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
s4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_7/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
s5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_7/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
s6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_7/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Add a source identifier to each to distinguish columns after union
# We will rename SalePrice column to match the target columns after union

s0 = s0.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_x"})
s1 = s1.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_y"})
s2 = s2.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_x_3"})
s3 = s3.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_y_4"})
s4 = s4.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_x_5"})
s6 = s6.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice_y_6"})

# Union the six sources vertically
unioned = pd.concat([s0, s1, s2, s3, s4, s6], ignore_index=True)

# Join unioned with s5 on Id
joined = pd.merge(unioned, s5, on="Id", how="inner", suffixes=("", "_s5"))

# s5's SalePrice corresponds to target's SalePrice column
joined = joined.rename(columns={"SalePrice": "SalePrice"})

# After join, multiple rows per Id exist (because unioned has multiple rows per Id from different sources)
# We need to pivot or aggregate to get one row per Id with all SalePrice columns

# The unioned table has only one SalePrice column per row, but different rows correspond to different SalePrice_* columns
# So we pivot the data to get columns SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y, etc. per Id

# But since unioned was concatenated vertically, each row has only one SalePrice_* column filled, others missing
# So pivoting by Id and aggregating max or mean per column will fill the columns

# First, group by Id and aggregate mean for each SalePrice_* column
agg_df = joined.groupby("Id").agg({
    "SalePrice_x": "mean",
    "SalePrice_y": "mean",
    "SalePrice_x_3": "mean",
    "SalePrice_y_4": "mean",
    "SalePrice_x_5": "mean",
    "SalePrice_y_6": "mean",
    "SalePrice": "mean"
}).reset_index()

# Write output with exact target schema column order
agg_df = agg_df[["Id", "SalePrice_x", "SalePrice_y", "SalePrice_x_3", "SalePrice_y_4", "SalePrice_x_5", "SalePrice_y_6", "SalePrice"]]

agg_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_7/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
